title: Words at War
paragraphs: NBC wartime anthology dramatizing contemporary books about World War II, produced with Council on Books in Wartime/war-information context.

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Anton M. Leader (director), Jack Costello (host and announcer), William Meeder (organ, performer, and composer), Morris Mamorsky (composer, conductor, and radio adaptor), Joseph Losey (director), Garnet Garrison (director), and Gerald Holland (radio adaptor and writer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]].
The stories often return to World War II, fascism and Nazism, wartime home front, military service and combat, occupation and resistance, and war aims and international affairs.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Council on Books in Wartime partnership, Office of War Information wartime context, and World War II contemporary-document adaptation.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]], [[show|the-chase|The Chase]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], and [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]].
